panel.title: Diagnosis
panel.description: The tool has matched the failure against the guide’s fault table (A–G). Work through the items in order, then go back to “Verify” and try again.
panel.redactedNote: API keys, tokens and other sensitive values are automatically redacted from the report, so it is safe to send to IT support.
panel.reportError: The diagnostic report could not be generated.

steps.whitespace: Check for stray spaces or line breaks at the beginning or end of the key; remove them and paste again.
steps.provider_selected: Make sure the newly added provider is the one “switched to / in use” in CC Switch, not another one.
steps.key_valid: Confirm on the platform that issued the key that it is valid (not expired, revoked or not yet activated).
steps.trailing_slash: Remove any extra trailing slash from the address (the tool strips it automatically, but double-check).
steps.v1_suffix: Check whether the address needs /v1: a bare host gets /v1 appended; an address that already has /v1 is used as-is.
steps.hash_literal: A trailing # means “use literally” — only use it when the gateway explicitly asks for it.
steps.close_all_terminals: Close every terminal window (Windows Terminal, PowerShell, CMD, Git Bash, macOS Terminal / iTerm).
steps.close_ide_terminals: Quit VS Code, Cursor and similar editors — their built-in terminals also carry the old environment.
steps.reopen_and_retry: Open a brand-new terminal window and verify again.
steps.inspect: On the “Environment” page, see where each variable comes from (registry, or which file and line).
steps.remove_manually: Remove or comment out those variables yourself following the instructions below — this tool never edits them.
steps.restart_terminal: Afterwards close every terminal window, open a new one and try again.
steps.check_npm_prefix_on_path: In a new terminal run npm prefix -g and make sure the printed directory (its bin subfolder on macOS) is on PATH.
steps.reinstall: If the command is still not found, go back to the “Install” step and reinstall.
steps.confirm_gateway_protocol: Confirm which protocol the gateway you are connecting to supports (the service gateway supports Responses).
steps.use_responses: Set the protocol to Responses in CC Switch.
steps.use_cc_switch_proxy: If the target only supports Chat Completions, enable the local proxy in CC Switch to convert the protocol.
steps.smartscreen_more_info: Windows: in the “Windows protected your PC” window click “More info”.
steps.gatekeeper_open_anyway: macOS: open “System Settings → Privacy & Security” and click “Open Anyway” at the bottom.
steps.remove_quarantine: Or run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AppName.app in Terminal.
steps.check_vpn_proxy: Check your VPN / proxy settings and that you are on the office network.
steps.try_mirror: If a download or install failed, switch to the intranet mirror and retry.
steps.retry: Wait a moment and try again.
steps.wait_retry: The gateway is temporarily busy or failing; wait a minute or two and retry.
steps.contact_support: If it keeps happening, export the diagnostic report and contact IT support.

key_checklist.title: Authentication failed: the gateway rejects your API key (401 / 403)
key_checklist.explanation: The gateway is reachable but refused the key. Almost always this is stray whitespace / line breaks from copy-paste, the wrong provider being active in CC Switch, or an invalid key. Check in order:

steps.whitespace: Stray spaces or line breaks: go back to CC Switch, delete the key and paste it again (pasting into a plain text editor first helps you see it).
steps.provider_selected: Wrong active provider: CC Switch may hold several providers, and the new one has to be “switched to / used” manually. Check which one is highlighted or ticked in the list.
steps.key_valid: The key itself: expired, revoked, not yet activated, or copied from another service. Confirm its status on the platform that issued it and request a new one if needed.

rule_recheck.title: Wrong address: the gateway returned 404
rule_recheck.explanation: The gateway is reachable but the path does not exist — usually a mistyped API address. Safest fix: go back to “Configure” and copy the address shown there exactly. Address rules:

steps.trailing_slash: A trailing slash is removed automatically — do not add one.
steps.v1_suffix: A bare host (e.g. https://gateway.example.com) gets /v1 appended automatically; an address that already has /v1 is used as-is.
steps.hash_literal: A trailing # means “use literally, append nothing” — only use it when the gateway explicitly asks for it.

restart_terminal.title: Configuration changed, but the terminal was not restarted
restart_terminal.explanation: Every terminal window copies the environment at the moment it opens and keeps using it, so terminals that are already open cannot see newly installed commands or new configuration. This is the most common problem in the whole guide.

steps.close_all_terminals: Close every terminal window: Windows Terminal, PowerShell, CMD, Git Bash, macOS Terminal / iTerm.
steps.close_ide_terminals: Quit VS Code, Cursor and similar editors entirely — their built-in terminals also carry the old environment.
steps.reopen_and_retry: Open a brand-new terminal window, come back here and click “Verify” again.

conflict.title: Environment variable conflict
conflict.explanation: Variables such as OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are set on this machine. Command-line tools prefer them and silently override what you configured in CC Switch. This tool only finds and locates them — it never edits them.

steps.inspect: On the “Environment” page, see where each variable comes from (Windows registry, or which file and line on macOS).
steps.remove_manually: Remove or comment out the variables yourself following the instructions below (note the values first if you may need them).
steps.restart_terminal: Then close every terminal window, open a new one and verify again.

instructions.windows:
Inspect and remove environment variables on Windows:
1. Right-click “This PC” → “Properties” → “Advanced system settings” → “Environment Variables”.
2. In both the “User variables” and “System variables” lists look for OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_BASE, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.
3. Select each one and click “Delete” (write the value down somewhere safe first if you might need it again). System variables may require administrator rights — ask IT.
4. Click “OK” to save, then close every terminal window and editor and open them again.
If the “Environment” page says a variable comes from your PowerShell profile ($PROFILE), open that file and delete or comment out the corresponding $env:… line.
instructions.macos:
Inspect and remove environment variables on macOS:
1. They usually live in ~/.zshrc or ~/.zprofile (bash users: ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bashrc). The “Environment” page tells you the exact file and line.
2. Open the file in a text editor (for example run open -e ~/.zshrc in Terminal).
3. Find lines like export OPENAI_API_KEY=… and delete them, or put # at the start of the line to comment them out, then save.
4. If a variable comes from launchctl, run launchctl unsetenv VARIABLE_NAME in Terminal.
5. Close every terminal window and editor and open them again.

not_refreshed.title: Command not found: PATH not refreshed or tool not installed
not_refreshed.explanation: The terminal reports “command not found” / “not recognized as an internal or external command”. Either the terminal was not restarted after installing, Node.js is missing or too old, or npm’s global bin directory is not on PATH.

steps.restart_terminal: Just installed and terminal not restarted: close every terminal window and editor, open a new one and try again.
steps.check_npm_prefix_on_path: In a new terminal run npm prefix -g and add the printed directory (on Windows the directory itself; on macOS its bin subfolder) to PATH. The tool shows the exact path.
steps.reinstall: Node.js missing / too old, or the command is still not found: go back to the “Install” step and reinstall.

mismatch.title: Protocol mismatch (400 / 422, or oddly formatted responses)
mismatch.explanation: Codex uses the Responses protocol; the service gateway supports and recommends Responses, so this normally does not happen. If you are connecting to another service that only supports Chat Completions, you need protocol conversion or a different address.

steps.confirm_gateway_protocol: Confirm which protocol the gateway you are connecting to supports (the service gateway supports Responses).
steps.use_responses: In the provider settings in CC Switch set the protocol to Responses, save and switch to it.
steps.use_cc_switch_proxy: If the target only supports Chat Completions, enable the local proxy in CC Switch for protocol conversion, or use an address that supports Responses.

app_blocked.title: Installer blocked by the operating system
app_blocked.explanation: Windows SmartScreen or macOS Gatekeeper blocked an unrecognised installer (“Windows protected your PC” / “cannot verify the developer”). Installers distributed by the company are signed and normally do not trigger this; if it keeps happening, download only from the intranet distribution point.

steps.smartscreen_more_info: Windows: in the “Windows protected your PC” window click “More info”.
steps.gatekeeper_open_anyway: macOS: open “System Settings → Privacy & Security” and click “Open Anyway” at the bottom of the page.
steps.remove_quarantine: Or run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AppName.app in Terminal to remove the quarantine flag.

instructions.windows:
When Windows SmartScreen blocks the installer:
1. In the blue “Windows protected your PC” window click the small “More info” link.
2. Click the “Run anyway” button that appears.
3. If double-clicking the installer does nothing at all: right-click it → “Properties” → tick “Unblock” at the bottom of the “General” tab → “OK”, then double-click again.
Only download installers from the company intranet distribution point or the official page.
instructions.macos:
When macOS Gatekeeper blocks the app:
1. Open “System Settings → Privacy & Security” and scroll down to the “Security” section.
2. Find the message “… was blocked” and click “Open Anyway”; confirm with your password.
3. If it says the app “is damaged and can’t be opened”: open Terminal and run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AppName.app (replace AppName with the real name, e.g. CC\ Switch), then open it again.
Only download installers from the company intranet distribution point or the official page.

unreachable.title: Network unreachable or request timed out
unreachable.explanation: The tool cannot reach the target (gateway, npm registry or GitHub). Usually you are not on the office network, VPN / proxy settings are wrong, or the target is temporarily unavailable.

steps.check_vpn_proxy: Make sure you are on the office network; check VPN / proxy settings (HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY).
steps.try_mirror: If a download or install failed, switch to the intranet mirror or npmmirror and retry.
steps.retry: Wait a moment and click “Verify” again.

upstream.title: Gateway temporarily busy or failing (429 / 5xx)
upstream.explanation: The address and key are most likely correct; the problem is on the gateway side — rate limiting because of too many requests, or a temporary upstream failure.

steps.wait_retry: Wait a minute or two and click “Verify” again.
steps.contact_support: If it keeps happening, export the diagnostic report and contact IT support.
